title: Ankhorage Orchestrator
summary: Executes deterministic install, configure, lifecycle, and uninstall actions for independently packaged project modules.
purpose: Provide a headless module lifecycle engine with explicit dependency ordering, state, actions, and rollback-aware file operations.
responsibilities: Define project modules and resolve their dependency graph.
Execute module lifecycle actions through explicit filesystem and process boundaries.
Record module state and ledger information for reconfiguration and uninstall.
Expose orchestration through package, CLI, and capability entrypoints.
boundaries: Does not own provider-specific module behavior or application UI.
Does not embed a particular hosting, package-manager, or deployment topology.
Does not bypass module dependency or lifecycle declarations with hidden global state.
audience: Module authors implementing deterministic project changes.
Tooling that installs, reconfigures, or removes project modules.
useCases: Install a dependency-ordered set of project modules.
Reconfigure modules from an explicit snapshot.
Uninstall a module using recorded lifecycle state.

architecture.role: Headless application engine coordinating module policy through filesystem and execution adapters.
invariants: Module ordering is derived from declared dependencies.
Lifecycle actions are deterministic for the same explicit project state.
Provider-specific modules remain separately packaged consumers of the engine.

limitations: Filesystem and command effects depend on the configured host environment.
Correct reversal depends on module actions recording sufficient lifecycle state.
